rules.statement: Never fabricate data. Placeholder metrics, invented deltas, and stock content are not evidence; use real product content or fixtures labelled as such.
rules.rationale: A screen built on invented numbers cannot be judged for hierarchy or interpretation, and it misleads whoever reviews it.

rules.statement: Status never relies on colour alone. Pair every status colour with text, an icon, or a shape that carries the same meaning.
rules.rationale: Colour-blind users, monochrome prints, and dim screens lose colour-only meaning; the pairing is the meaning.

rules.statement: Essential actions stay visible and named. Do not hide the next action behind hover, overflow, or an icon without an accessible name.
rules.rationale: An action the user cannot find or a screen reader cannot announce does not exist for them.

rules.statement: Controls keep visible labels, readable contrast, a visible focus state, keyboard order that follows visual order, and a safe way to recover from errors.
rules.rationale: Operability is the floor under every aesthetic decision; a suppressed focus ring or an unlabeled field breaks the task for keyboard and assistive-technology users.
rules.anchor: Preserve labels, contrast, focus, keyboard access, and safe recovery.

rules.statement: Semantic roles (accent, status, canvas, type roles) do not change between screens without a recorded decision. Unexplained local variation is not a role.
rules.rationale: Drift between screens is how a design system dissolves. The decisions ledger (decisions[] in .styleseed/project.json; ss-resolve/references/decisions.md) records the decided values and approved exceptions. drift-report.mjs --gate measures rendered screens and exits 3 on at-rest drift in accent, ink, canvas, or spacing base, or on a value outside a recorded decision; the spacing scale, type sizes, radii, fonts, and control heights are listed and fail only against a decision.

rules.statement: Use semantic tokens for stable action, status, category, brand, and content roles. Hardcoded colours live only in registered token or theme files.
exceptions: one-off illustration or chart series colours declared as tokens in the artifact's token files
rules.rationale: A colour named by its role can be changed in one place and checked against contrast; a literal cannot.
rules.anchor: Use semantic tokens for stable action, status, category, brand, and content roles

rules.statement: Reuse the approved spacing scale. Without one, start from {4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96} and record any optical, script, canvas, or platform adjustment.
rules.rationale: A shared scale is what makes grouping legible across screens; arbitrary pixel values are the first visible drift.

rules.statement: Motion uses one duration and easing family, names the properties it transitions, communicates state or sequence, never delays the first read, and provides a complete reduced-motion result.
rules.rationale: transition-all and missing reduced-motion paths are the two ways motion stops being a decision and becomes noise.

rules.statement: Buttons, inputs, and selects in one context share a height. Touch surfaces provide at least 44px targets; pointer-first dense desktop controls may be smaller when still operable.
exceptions: inline text controls inside dense tables when the row itself is the target
rules.rationale: Mixed control heights read as several products on one screen. drift-report.mjs --gate enforces heights only once the project has recorded a controlHeights decision in its decisions ledger: a rendered control height outside the decided set and its approved exceptions exits 3. Without a decision the report lists the control-height families per screen and does not fail.

rules.statement: Navigation, status, and action symbols come from the project's icon family with accessible labels; emoji are content, not icons.
rules.rationale: Emoji glyphs differ per platform and ignore the project's icon system. drift-report.mjs --faults reports an emoji-only element inside a control, leading a row, or alone in a small tile as emoji-icon. It cannot tell a reaction from an icon, so it reports and never fails the gate.

rules.statement: Icons in one navigation, list, or toolbar come from one family; outline and filled variants coexist only to mark state.
exceptions: coordinated outline and filled variants that mark the selected state
rules.rationale: Two icon families on one bar read as two products. drift-report.mjs --faults lists the icon signatures per screen (viewBox grid and stroke or fill construction) and reports a group that mixes them as icon-mix. Brand marks look like a second family, so it reports and never fails the gate.

rules.statement: Inside consumer-service cards, 2–4 options use a pill toggle and 5 or more move to a dedicated page. Native selects, radio groups, and checkbox filters stay valid under other contracts.
exceptions: settings pages, forms, and dense consoles use native controls and keep platform behaviour (§18)
rules.rationale: In a mobile card the pill keeps the choice visible and the touch target large; the same control inside a settings form would hide the platform semantics people expect.

rules.statement: In consumer-service dashboards, content lives inside cards; only TopBar, BottomNav, and carousel titles sit outside. Flat reading flow, selectable rows, and uncarded sections are valid under other contracts.
exceptions: operations consoles, editorial pages, and settings forms (DESIGN-LANGUAGE §18, METHODOLOGY §2)
rules.rationale: The card is the recipe's unit of rhythm on a phone; forcing it onto a dense console doubles the chrome without adding grouping.

rules.statement: Displayed amounts never wrap mid-value. Keep the sign, number, and unit on one line (whitespace-nowrap) for hero metrics, KPI metrics, list amounts, chart prices, donut centres, and storage quantities.
rules.rationale: A value split across lines reads as two values; the eye locks onto magnitude first and loses it at the break. drift-report.mjs --faults measures rendered screens: an element whose whole text is one amount and that is laid out on two or more lines is reported as amount-wrap.

rules.statement: Product UI copy uses a friendly, conversational voice by default. Regulated or legal copy follows UX-WRITING.md and keeps the same clarity.
exceptions: legal, medical, and financial disclosures with mandated wording
rules.rationale: Plain language lowers the cost of every decision the interface asks for; mandated wording is the one place it yields.

rules.statement: Numbers lead and units follow small: set a value at about twice the size of its unit so magnitude reads first, and always use thousands separators.
exceptions: tabular columns where every cell shares one unit shown in the header
rules.rationale: Equal sizes flatten value and unit into one token; the ratio is what makes a metric scannable.

rules.statement: Loading skeletons match the shape of the final content (same padding, radius, and text heights); no spinner inside a card. Show a skeleton after a 300ms delay and keep it for at least 300ms.
exceptions: sub-200ms responses that never show a loading state
rules.rationale: A skeleton that matches the layout keeps the reader's place; a spinner or an empty card that fills later makes the screen jump twice.
rules.anchor: Skeletons match the shape of final content

rules.statement: Empty and error states stay in place: a failing card shows its own error while the rest renders; zero displays as 0, never as a dash; every message names the problem and a recovery.
exceptions: a full-page failure uses the full-screen error pattern
rules.rationale: Partial failure handled locally preserves the rest of the decision; hiding a zero or a failure behind a dash hides the state the user needs to act on.

rules.statement: Negative amounts use a minus sign (-$1.8K), never parentheses, and the destructive text role; at zero use the default text colour and no trend icon.
exceptions: accounting exports that must follow a client's statement format
rules.rationale: The minus sign reads in every locale and font; parentheses are an accounting convention most product users do not share.

rules.statement: CJK text breaks at word boundaries, a number stays on one line with its CJK unit, and Pretendard's tall ascender is corrected only at 36px and above.
rules.rationale: Mid-syllable breaks and orphaned numbers are the most common Korean typography tells in generated UI.

rules.statement: The number of visible items follows the decision, the available width, the labels, and the input mode. There is no universal four-item limit; dense rows and small multiples are valid.
rules.rationale: A fixed item quota optimises for one phone dashboard; monitoring and editing tasks need coordinated dense regions immediately.
rules.anchor: There is no universal four-item card limit

rules.statement: In the consumer-service recipe, shadows stay between 4% and 12% opacity: subtle depth, not a floating card.
exceptions: overlays and sheets that must separate from the page
rules.rationale: Heavy shadows multiply across a card grid and compete with the content they were meant to lift.

rules.statement: In consumer-service cards, hover and click effects belong to controls, not to cards or list rows; no swipe gestures outside carousels and no long-press menus.
exceptions: selectable rows in consoles and lists where the row is the action (§18)
rules.rationale: A card that reacts to hover promises an action it does not have; the recipe keeps affordance on the controls.

rules.statement: In the consumer-service recipe, type is set by role on the five-level scale (display, headline, title, body, label/caption), and category labels are uppercase with tracking.
exceptions: an approved project type scale replaces the recipe's sizes while keeping the roles
rules.rationale: Roles travel across screens; raw sizes do not. The drift report compares type sizes per screen for the same reason.

rules.statement: List status uses a same-colour dot together with same-colour text; the dot never carries the status alone.
rules.rationale: The recipe's way of satisfying the status invariant (INV-02) inside dense list rows.
